conviction_note: Quarter-end and October NAV are already public (Sep 30 est. midpoint $4.04, Oct 31 est. $3.85-3.91), so the print adds NII, buyback activity and the call's distribution commentary. A peer relief rally (ECC +9.4% the session after a NAV-down print) and a 19% discount to the October NAV pull one way. A distribution running at roughly 150% of last quarter's NII, at a time when peers' CLO equity cash yields are compressing (OXLC halved its payout), pulls the other. The findings net to about +0.2 and the scaled number is +0.27 (p_up 53 x abs 4.5). The fundamental read (NII below a disputed $0.19-0.21 bar) is negative while the reaction lean is slightly positive, because NII is not the line this closed-end fund trades on.
bar: NII/EPS consensus $0.19 (Earnings Whispers preview, 2026-11-11, https://finviz.com/news/421326/ellington-credit-faces-a-credibility-test-as-shares-slide-toward-post-earnings-lows) vs $0.21 (Chartmill, https://www.chartmill.com/stock/quote/EARN/estimates); the two sources disagree, so the bar is disputed and the NII finding is capped small. Revenue consensus about $9.4M vs $12.0M last quarter (EW). Prior quarter (Jun) NII $0.16 GAAP / $0.15 adjusted, distributions $0.24/quarter. No company guidance exists. For a CLO closed-end fund the line that usually matters is NAV, which is pre-released: Sep 30 est. $4.01-4.07 (497AD 2026-10-16) and Oct 31 est. $3.85-3.91 (497AD 2026-11-18).
positioning_check: Short interest about 370,200 shares, 0.9 days to cover (ShortSqueeze snapshot 2026-11-11, https://shortsqueeze.com/?symbol=EARN). Other sources show 752K / 2.9 days at the 2026-09-30 settlement (https://massive.com/quote/earn) and about 2-3% of float in mid-October (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/EARN/short-interest). Not crowded, so it gives no squeeze mechanism. No usable option chain ('no_paired_strikes'), so there is no skew. The tape: spot $3.145 at the 52-week low, -12.15% over 20 days, -44.8% from the 52-week high, and a 19% discount to the Oct 31 NAV midpoint against 0% at Sep 30 and -10.3% at Oct 31.

findings.finding: ECC, the closest listed CLO-equity peer, reported its Sep quarter on 2026-11-12. Its NAV fell from $4.51 to $4.17 and it guided October to $3.73-3.83 (about -9% more). Its CEO called the drop in CLO arbitrage 'at a minimum a medium-term shift'. ECC still rose +9.4% the next session (2.13 to 2.33) and stood at 2.46 by 2026-11-19. Over the same days EARN drifted from 3.21 to 3.165 and has had no relief move of its own.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: EARN's own last eight prints moved a median 2.2%, 6 of 8 up, and the last four were all up (+2.07, +3.23, +2.29, +0.59): the stock has tended to rise on prints that clear away NAV uncertainty. After the Aug print it then drifted -23.5% (Earnings Whispers).
findings.why_not_priced: If the market were already pricing a sector-wide relief on 'bad but known' NAV prints, EARN would have bounced with ECC after 2026-11-12. It did not: it is 1.5% lower while ECC is 15% higher. ECC prices: https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/ECC?range=1mo&interval=1d; EARN prices: https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/EARN?range=2mo&interval=1d
findings.independence: This is a peer reaction (same asset class, same week), not EARN's own number. The link is that both are listed CLO-equity closed-end funds with pre-released monthly NAV estimates. EARN holds about 43% CLO debt, which is less volatile than ECC's equity-heavy book. Price data: https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/ECC?range=1mo&interval=1d

findings.finding: The distribution looks large against income, and the Nov 20 call is inside the window. EARN pays $0.08 a month ($0.24 a quarter; the Dec 31 payment was declared 2026-11-05) against Jun-quarter adjusted NII of $0.15, roughly 63% coverage. That is about 30% a year on the $3.145 spot and about 25% on the Oct NAV. Peers show the same compression in CLO equity cash yields: OXLC's cash distribution yield fell from 16.3% to 12.4% and it halved its monthly payout to $0.10 (release 2026-11-05). EARN fell 8.2% that day (3.43 to 3.15) and ECC fell 13.7%. The call could address whether the payout is sustainable.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There are no EARN reactions on record to a distribution change under the closed-end fund structure. On 2026-11-05 the sector sold off on OXLC's cut, and EARN fell 8.2% on a peer's payout news alone.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: a 30% trailing yield already implies a cut. What is not priced is management saying so on the call. The next declaration falls in early December, outside the window, so in-window the risk is only the call's commentary. If a cut were fully priced, the stock would not have fallen 8% on a peer's cut.
findings.independence: The EARN distribution comes from its own 8-K/Business Wire (https://finviz.com/news/417852/ellington-credit-declares-monthly-common-distribution, 2026-11-05) and the Jun-quarter NII from https://www.quiverquant.com/news/Ellington+Credit+reports+%2412.3+million+GAAP+net+income+for+June+quarter. ECC extended its $0.06 monthly payout through Q1 2027 (finviz 422707), which points the other way and was rewarded.

findings.finding: The NII consensus is $0.19 (EW) or $0.21 (Chartmill), against $0.15 adjusted / $0.16 GAAP last quarter. Consensus revenue is $9.4M, against $12.0M last quarter. Peers' CLO-equity effective yields fell this quarter: ECC from 9.0% to 8.4%, OXLC from 11.1% to 10.5%. A step up in EARN's NII is therefore against the sector trend, and a miss on the EPS line is more likely than a beat.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: EARN missed Q1 2026 EPS ($0.19 vs about $0.245) and the reaction was +3.23% (2026-05-20), so it has not traded on the EPS line.
findings.why_not_priced: The consensus implies a 27% rise in NII from last quarter. If the market believed peers' yield compression applied to EARN, the consensus would sit at or below $0.15-0.16. Capped small because the bar is disputed between two sources.
findings.independence: The peer yields come from different documents: ECC (finviz 422707) and OXLC (finviz 416899). It is a proxy: EARN has not reported its own Q3 yield.

findings.finding: On 2026-10-09 the board authorised a $20M buyback (about 14% of the $137M market cap). Shares outstanding were 39.5mm on both the Sep 30 and Oct 31 fact sheets, so essentially nothing was repurchased in October. The stock has since sunk to a 19% discount to the Oct 31 NAV midpoint ($3.88), where buybacks would add NAV per share. The release and call can disclose November repurchases or a commitment to buy.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock rose from 3.41 to 3.74 over the two weeks after the 2026-10-09 authorisation (8-K filed 2026-10-16), then gave it all back.
findings.why_not_priced: Unchanged share counts in two primary fact sheets show the authorisation has not been used, so the market has had no buying support. If repurchases were expected, the discount would not have widened from 10% to 19% in November.
findings.independence: The share counts come from the 497AD of 2026-10-16 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1560672/000199937126022873/earn-497ad_101626.htm) and of 2026-11-18 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1560672/000199937126025673/earn-497ad_111726.htm), both different documents from the 8-K.

findings.finding: The quarter's NAV is fully pre-released: Sep 30 est. $4.01-4.07 (stock then at 0% discount) and Oct 31 est. $3.85-3.91 (stock $3.48, -10.3%; filed 2026-11-18). At $3.145 the stock trades at a 19% discount to the October midpoint, having fallen 9.6% in November with no new NAV published. A release that confirms quarter-end NAV near $4.04 and carries no new markdown removes one source of uncertainty.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Aug print (NAV also pre-released via July estimate) moved +2.07%, then the stock drifted -23.5% over the following weeks.
findings.why_not_priced: The NAV number itself is priced, so only the discount is in play. The November decline may reflect further CLO equity markdowns that the release could confirm with a later estimate, which is why this is sized small and toward 0.
findings.independence: The Sep 30 estimate comes from a separate 497AD (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1560672/000199937126022873/earn-497ad_101626.htm). The discount argument is close to the ECC relief finding in spirit but rests on EARN's own documents.

findings.finding: On 2026-10-23 EARN signed a $125M at-the-market equity distribution agreement (Citizens JMP, B. Riley, Lucid, Armstrong; up to 2% commission) for general corporate purposes and new investments. A 1940-Act closed-end fund generally cannot sell below NAV, so at a 19% discount the ATM cannot be used and creates no supply overhang.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock rose from 3.58 to 3.74 over the days around the ATM filing (2026-10-22 to 10-27), so there was no adverse reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: What the money buys is growth while the fund trades at or above NAV, which is not the case now, so the agreement is near zero in the window. It only matters if management signals asset growth ahead of buybacks.

outside_window.finding: The next monthly distribution declaration (January 2027 payment) is due around early December, going by the 2026-10-07 and 2026-11-05 declaration dates. That is where a cut would actually be announced.

searched_and_found_nothing: An October/November 2026 analyst rating change or price-target cut: none dated in the window found (Fintel median target $5.10 as of 2026-10-02, Piper Sandler Overweight 2026-07-13)
A November 2026 leveraged-loan or CLO-equity price level: index pages only, no numbers
Cause of the 2026-10-05 to 10-07 heavy-volume drop (4.03 to 3.48): no company filing on those dates beyond the 2026-10-07 distribution 8-K
Q2 call transcript (marketbeat 403); management commentary only through an AI summary (panabee), not used for numbers

rejected_candidates.candidate: Earnings Whispers bullish sentiment rising to 59.9% from 8.3% before the previous report
rejected_candidates.detail: The same EW preview document as the NII-bar finding; a sentiment survey with no mechanism, folded into positioning_check context rather than filed.
Superseded by the primary 497AD estimates for Sep 30 and Oct 31, which carry the NAV finding.

baseline_tension: The baseline has no skew. The 20-day run-up of -12% and the widening discount sit with the negative (distribution) finding, which is mostly priced, while the peer relief rally cuts against the run-up. With no usable chain, the lean stays near 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 6 (bar unsourced or disputed): EW $0.19 against Chartmill $0.21, so the NII finding is capped small, from -0.6 to -0.5.

Lesson 5 (an unexplained drawdown is worth 0) and the core rule on pre-released periods: the NAV-discount finding goes from +0.8 to +0.3, because the quarter's NAV is pre-released and the November slide is partly explained by OXLC's cut.
Lesson 3 (own caveat reaches the number): the distribution finding admits a 30% yield already prices a cut, so it goes from -1.2 to -1.0.
Lesson 4 (financing is a question): ATM asked what it buys, unusable below NAV, kept at 0.
Lesson 1 (verified fact vs reaction): this name rose on its Q1 EPS miss, so print_vs_bar (-12%) does not set the sign of the reaction; p_up stays near 50 (53).
What worked (a peer printing after the company last spoke): ECC finding left at +1.0.
